AI Overview

When choosing running shoes for flat feet (low arches), the key is managing overpronation (when your foot rolls too far inward) and finding the right mix of support, cushioning, and a broad base.

What to Look For
  • Stability or Guided Support: Look for terms like GuideRails®, 4D Guidance, or dual-density midsoles rather than rigid hard-plastic arch lumps. (Note: Some runners with mild flat feet do fine in well-cushioned neutral shoes like the
    Brooks Ghost Max
    Go to product viewer dialog for this item.
    or
    ASICS Gel-Nimbus
    Go to product viewer dialog for this item.
    if they do not overpronate severely    .)     
  • Wide/Accommodating Base: Flat feet often spread or require extra width. Check if the brand offers wide (2E) sizing. 
  • Firm Heel Counter: A stiffer back heel helps keep your heel bone aligned and stops it from collapsing sideways. 
  • Toe Room: Leave about a thumb's width of space at the front so your toes aren't crammed. 
To help narrow down the best pair, let me know:
  • Are you looking for daily road training, walking, or race day?
  • Do you know if you overpronate heavily or experience foot/knee pain?
  • Do you prefer a softer/plush ride or a firmer/supportive feel?
